::: {.why}
The rank deficiency you counted last night is not an edge case; it is the normal situation in equity portfolio construction, and every practical method exists because of it.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the rank of a sample covariance matrix from T observations of N assets, and what that implies for its inverse.
- Show that the sample matrix produces a portfolio with zero predicted risk and large realised risk.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Demonstrate the failure end to end: with 200 names and 150 days, find a portfolio the sample covariance says has almost zero variance, then measure what it actually realises over the next 150 days. The ratio between predicted and realised risk is the number to remember.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Map the breakdown: repeat with the ratio of assets to observations from 0.1 to 1.5 and plot predicted-to-realised risk against that ratio. The curve tells you where your own universe sits and how bad the problem is for you specifically.
:::
:::
